n: The Spirit carries Ezekiel to the temple’s east gate, where twenty-five leaders are gathered, including Jaazaniah son of Azur (a different man from 8:11) and Pelatiah son of Benaiah.

f.w: five and twenty men
princes of the people
f.g: Civic leaders and officials of Jerusalem.

n: These men plot evil and give the city wicked advice.

f.w: devise mischief

n: They say: “Destruction isn’t near; let’s build houses. This city is the cooking pot and we are the meat”—meaning they are the choice cuts, safe inside the walls, while the exiles were the scraps thrown away.

f.w: It is not near; let us build houses
f.g: Possibly the opposite of Jeremiah’s advice to the exiles to build houses in Babylon.

f.w: caldron

n: God tells Ezekiel to prophesy against them—twice, for emphasis.

f.w: prophesy, O son of man

n: The Spirit falls on Ezekiel. God knows every thought that crosses their minds.

f.w: I know the things that come into your mind

n: These leaders have filled Jerusalem’s streets with murdered people through their injustice.

f.w: Ye have multiplied your slain

n: God turns their saying around: the only “meat” safe in the pot is the innocent people they killed. The leaders themselves will be dragged out.

f.w: they are the flesh
f.g: The victims, not the leaders, are the true choice portion.

n: They feared the sword, so the sword will come upon them.

f.w: Ye have feared the sword

n: God will remove them from the city and hand them over to foreigners for judgment.

f.w: deliver you into the hands of strangers

n: They will die at Israel’s border. This was fulfilled when Nebuchadnezzar executed Judah’s leaders at Riblah, at the northern edge of the land.

f.w: I will judge you in the border of Israel

n: Jerusalem will not protect them like a pot protects meat; judgment will meet them at the border.

f.w: This city shall not be your caldron

n: They will know the Lord, because instead of following his laws they copied the ways of the surrounding nations.

f.w: have done after the manners of the heathen

n: As Ezekiel prophesies in vision, Pelatiah suddenly dies—perhaps at the same moment in Jerusalem. Shaken, Ezekiel falls down and cries out: will God destroy the whole remnant?

f.w: Pelatiah
f.g: His name ironically means “The LORD rescues.”

f.w: wilt thou make a full end of the remnant

n: God answers with a new message—one of hope.

f.w: Again the word of the LORD came unto me
f.g: A turn from judgment to promise.

n: Jerusalem’s residents scorn the exiles: “They are far from the Lord; the land is ours now.” But God says the exiles are Ezekiel’s true brothers and the real heirs of the promise.

f.w: Get you far from the LORD
f.g: They assumed being in Jerusalem meant being close to God.

f.w: unto us is this land given in possession

n: One of the most comforting verses in Ezekiel: though God scattered them, he himself will be “a little sanctuary” for them in exile. God’s presence is not limited to a building or a land.

f.w: a little sanctuary
f.g: Or “a sanctuary for a little while.” Jewish tradition connects this to the synagogue.

n: God promises to gather the scattered and give them the land of Israel again—a theme of latter-day gathering that Latter-day Saints emphasize.

f.w: I will even gather you
f.r: Ezekiel 36:24; Jeremiah 32:37; 1 Nephi 22:12; Articles of Faith 1:10

n: When they return, they will remove all the idols and abominations from the land.

f.w: they shall take away all the detestable things

n: The heart of the promise: God will give his people one heart and a new spirit, replacing a stony, unfeeling heart with a heart of flesh—responsive and alive. This is a picture of spiritual rebirth.

f.w: one heart
I will put a new spirit within you
stony heart

n: The new heart leads to obedience, and obedience restores the covenant relationship: “they shall be my people, and I will be their God.”

f.w: they shall be my people, and I will be their God

n: But those whose hearts stay devoted to their idols will receive the consequences of their own conduct.

f.w: whose heart walketh after the heart of their detestable things
f.g: Whose loyalty stays with their idols.

n: The cherubim lift their wings, with the wheels and God’s glory above them. The departure continues.

f.w: the glory of the God of Israel was over them

n: God’s glory leaves the city entirely and rests on the mountain east of Jerusalem—the Mount of Olives. Prophecy and the New Testament connect this mountain with the Lord’s coming again.

f.w: the mountain which is on the east side of the city

n: The Spirit returns Ezekiel in vision to the exiles in Babylonia, and the vision ends.

f.w: Chaldea

n: Ezekiel tells the exiles everything the Lord showed him—both the judgment on Jerusalem and the promise of a new heart.

f.w: all the things that the LORD had shewed me
